name: Indiana

law.summary: Every Indiana CSO community must notify the affected public, people who asked in response to its annual March newspaper notice, local health departments and drinking-water intakes within 10 river miles downstream whenever a CSO is occurring or imminent, in a manner agreed with the recipient, and post warning signs; no web channel or deadline is set. Great Lakes basin CSO permittees also owe the 4-hour notice of 40 CFR 122.38 (327 IAC 5-2.2). SSOs and bypasses are reported only to IDEM.

citations.title: CSO notification: who and when
citations.quote: Notification must be provided whenever information from a reliable source indicates that: (1) a discharge or discharges from one (1) or more combined sewer overflow outfalls is occurring; or (2) a discharge or discharges from one (1) or more combined sewer overflow outfalls is imminent based on predicted or actual precipitation or a related event.
citations.channel: affected public; persons who request it; local health departments; drinking water suppliers with intakes within 10 river miles downstream
citations.threshold: any CSO discharge occurring or imminent

citations.title: Community notification methods
citations.quote: Provide public notice in a newspaper of general circulation in March of each year to allow the following to request receipt of CSO notification ... Provide notification to those ... who request receipt of CSO notification ... in a manner that is mutually agreeable to the recipient and the CSO community.
citations.channel: annual newspaper notice; then email/phone/other as agreed; prominent signs at access points

citations.title: Great Lakes Basin CSO public notification
citations.quote: The requirements of this rule and 40 CFR 122.38 apply to a permittee authorized to discharge a combined sewer overflow to the Great Lakes Basin.
citations.who: CSO permittees in the Lake Michigan and Lake Erie basins

cso.notification_practice: Opt-in notice by email or phone to people who answer an annual March newspaper notice, plus signs. Public web traces only at LaPorte (status page), Waterloo and Goshen (posts). Indianapolis sends forecast-based email warnings; South Bend and Hammond email on request; Fort Wayne, Mishawaka, Kendallville and Speedway pages blocked scripted access.

sso.notes: SSOs reported to IDEM on State Form 48373; Highland posts its forms as PDFs.

readiness.rationale: No statewide event list and the rule needs no web posting. A few small operators post dated events (LaPorte, Waterloo, Goshen), but the large systems notify by email on request or block scripted access. Build on the IDEM outfall layer, ECHO monthly CSO DMRs and the rain caution; email subscriptions (Citizens, South Bend, Hammond) could lift Indiana to B.

owner_questions: Subscribe to the Citizens, South Bend, Hammond and Speedway CSO emails? This needs the owner to phone or mail requests, and Citizens' route is unknown.
Can forecast-based 'imminent CSO' emails (Indianapolis) be shown at all? They are warnings, not reports of a discharge.
Use IDEM's outfall layer instead of EPA's inventory for Indiana (981 vs 671 open)?
Create an Access Indiana account for BeachAlert alerts, or rely on Swim Guide?
surprise: Indiana's rule makes CSO notice opt-in: each CSO community invites requests through a March newspaper ad and then notifies requesters 'in a manner that is mutually agreeable'. Indianapolis (131 open outfalls) sends email warnings when rain is forecast rather than when an overflow is measured, so the state's biggest CSO system leaves no public web record of events.
